tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/internal-http.md <<'EOF'
# Plain HTTP for internal hosts

The project's current recorded decision is HTTPS everywhere, with no plaintext exception: internal hosts are held to the same rule as any other host and must be reached over HTTPS, not plain HTTP. The stated reason is that proper certificate management is now in place.
EOF
cat docs/policies/internal-http.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/internal-http.md`. It says the current decision is HTTPS everywhere with no plaintext exception, so internal hosts follow the same rule as any other host. It gives the reason as proper certificate management now being in place.

Muninn has two related records. The earlier one allowed plain HTTP for internal hosts. The later one (#34) reversed it, so I used only the later one and left the earlier stance out of the file. Both are recorded as transcript excerpts (trust 1), not as formal decisions.

The first attempt to write the file through Bash failed on a heredoc parse error. I used the Write tool instead, and the file was created.
